purpose: Record internet-verified Nigerian skills, competency and certification anchors before any SQL or seed regeneration.

scope.note: A body or government page is not treated as proof of a professional licence unless the source explicitly establishes regulation, registration, examination or certification.

verified_sources.name: Computer Professionals Registration Council of Nigeria, 2021 Examination Syllabus
verified_claims: The CPN examination is a route into recognised IT professional practice in Nigeria.
The syllabus is intended to sustain competence and skills across the Nigerian computing and ICT industry.
verified_sources.domain_signal: ICT, data, AI, cloud, cybersecurity, IoT, telecommunications and digital-production domains

verified_sources.name: Nigeria Computer Society
verified_claims: NCS describes itself as the umbrella body for Nigerian IT professionals and interest groups.
Its current programmes cover AI, robotics, cybersecurity, fintech, IoT, digital learning and computing education.
verified_sources.domain_signal: ICT, AI, cyber, fintech, robotics, IoT and computing education

verified_sources.name: National Board for Technical Education, NSQF and National Occupational Standards
verified_claims: NSQF defines skills, knowledge, understanding and competencies regardless of where learning occurred.
NBTE publishes National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualifications routes.
verified_sources.domain_signal: technical, vocational, craft, construction, ICT and trade domains

verified_sources.name: Council for Innovative Engineering and Emerging Engineering in Nigeria
verified_claims: The council lists professional categories from engineer to craftsman and describes structured certification and standards.
Its listed specialisations include AI, big data, blockchain, biomedical, clean energy, IoT, machine learning, robotics, quantum and telecommunications.
certifications: structured professional certification categories listed by the council
verified_sources.domain_signal: emerging engineering, AI, robotics, telecoms, energy and automation

verified_sources.name: Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, Nigeria
verified_claims: The ministry identifies Nigerian health regulatory bodies and its mandate includes health policy, quality services and regulation of institutions and professionals.
certifications: No profession-specific credential is inferred from this ministry page; the relevant council must supply it.
verified_sources.domain_signal: medicine, nursing, pharmacy, public health and allied-health context

verified_sources.name: Medical Laboratory Science Council of Nigeria
verified_claims: MLSCN regulates medical laboratory science and sets the standard of knowledge and skill for scientists, technicians and assistants.
It conducts examinations and maintains separate professional registers.
competencies: meet Council knowledge and skill standards
operate within laboratory approval and inspection requirements
certifications: MLSCN registration categories for scientists, technicians and assistants
Council examinations for technicians and assistants
verified_sources.domain_signal: medical laboratory and allied-health domains

verified_sources.name: Council for the Regulation of Engineering in Nigeria, Construction Labour Market Information System
verified_claims: CORBON publishes National Occupational Standards for Nigerian building trades to address construction skills gaps.
The published standards cover electrical installation, carpentry and joinery, masonry, painting and decoration, and plumbing.
competencies: perform construction work to defined occupational standards
verified_sources.domain_signal: construction and building-trade domains

verified_sources.name: Quantity Surveyors Registration Board of Nigeria
verified_claims: QSRBN regulates and controls quantity surveying practice in Nigeria and registers individuals and firms.
Registration requires relevant education, professional certificates, supervised experience and induction.
verified_sources.domain_signal: quantity surveying and built-environment domains

verified_sources.name: Nigerian Nuclear Regulatory Authority
verified_claims: NNRA registers, licences, inspects and enforces nuclear safety and radiological protection in Nigeria.
Radiation Safety Officers need relevant education, training, accredited radiation-protection examination and supervised on-the-job training.
certifications: NNRA-accredited radiation-protection course and RSO accreditation requirements
verified_sources.domain_signal: radiation, nuclear, medical physics and imaging domains

verified_sources.name: Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria
verified_claims: TRCN establishes teacher standards, approves qualifications, registers and licenses teachers, and administers the Professional Qualifying Examination.
The current PQE curriculum names pedagogy, literacy, numeracy, ICT and safeguarding as core areas.
verified_sources.domain_signal: teaching, education administration and learning-support domains

verified_sources.name: Nigerian Oil and Gas Industry Content Joint Qualification System
verified_claims: NOGIC-JQS maintains individual and company competency searches and validates NCDMB-approved certifications in the Nigerian oil and gas industry.
The system is intended as a national skills-development pool and includes certificate verification.
certifications: NCEC, NCRC, NCTRC and marine-vessel categorization certificates
verified_sources.domain_signal: energy, petroleum, offshore, marine, engineering and industrial-safety domains

verified_sources.name: Centre for Management Development, Nigeria
verified_claims: CMD is the operational arm of the Nigerian Council for Management Development and supports management training, consultancy, research and education.
Its published values include integrity, professionalism and excellence.
certifications: CMD professional training and certification renewal signals; exact credential names require programme-level verification
verified_sources.domain_signal: management, administration, entrepreneurship and business domains

verified_sources.name: National Space Research and Development Agency
verified_claims: NASRDA has institutes and departments covering space science, space engineering, satellite systems and related technology development.
competencies: work with satellite and remote-sensing systems
certifications: No Nigerian professional licence is inferred from NASRDA pages; use academic and engineering regulators separately.
verified_sources.domain_signal: space technology and space science domains

verified_sources.name: National Emergency Management Agency
verified_claims: NEMA is the Nigerian national emergency-management source for preparedness, response, relief and recovery coordination.
certifications: No statutory professional credential is inferred from the NEMA homepage; training credentials require source-specific confirmation.
verified_sources.domain_signal: humanitarian aid, emergency response and public-safety domains

verified_sources.name: Federal Ministry of Arts, Culture, Creative Economy and Social Development
verified_claims: The ministry provides Nigerian creative-economy, entertainment and gaming sector context; it is not a professional licensing body.
certifications: No professional credential is inferred from the ministry pages.
verified_sources.domain_signal: media, performing arts, games, fashion and creative-economy domains

verified_sources.name: Institute of Chartered Accountants of Nigeria, 2026 syllabus
verified_claims: ICAN's professional syllabus is organised into Foundation, Skills and Professional levels and states learning outcomes and competences.
The qualification combines technical knowledge, professional judgement, ethics, communication and practical experience.
verified_sources.domain_signal: accounting, finance, audit, tax, investment and credit domains

verified_sources.name: Chartered Institute of Bankers of Nigeria competency framework
verified_claims: CIBN is the Nigerian banking profession body and is appointed under the banking competency framework to accredit training and certification.
Its examination material includes business communication, economics, accounting, finance, management, business law and ethics, ICT and quantitative techniques.
competencies: meet banking knowledge and skill standards
certifications: Associateship of the Chartered Institute of Bankers (ACIB)
verified_sources.domain_signal: banking, credit, fintech, finance and financial-risk domains

verified_sources.name: Nigeria Union of Journalists code and registration resources
verified_claims: NUJ's code requires truth, accuracy, fairness, privacy, confidentiality, public interest and copyright-aware practice.
NUJ lists training, education and adherence to its ethics code among its professional functions.
competencies: report fairly and in the public interest
certifications: NUJ membership and professional registration signals; no statutory licence inferred
verified_sources.domain_signal: journalism, media production, communications and translation context

verified_sources.name: Nigerian Library Association and Librarians Registration Council context
verified_claims: NLA supports capacity building and standards for education and certification of librarians, archivists and information scientists.
The association identifies LRCN as the Nigerian practice regulator and supports lifelong learning, digital transformation and information literacy.
verified_sources.domain_signal: library, archive, information science and research domains

verified_sources.name: Nigerian Council of Food Science and Technology
verified_claims: NiCFoST regulates the practice and profession of Food Science and Technology in Nigeria.
The Council requires registration as a Certified Food Scientist of Nigeria and an annual practice licence for practice.
verified_sources.domain_signal: food science, nutrition, food production and hospitality domains

verified_sources.name: NIHOTOUR RIVAC registration portal
verified_claims: NIHOTOUR's portal describes registration, identification, verification, accreditation and certification for Nigerian hospitality, travel and tourism personnel and operators.
competencies: work within tourism and hospitality compliance requirements
certifications: RIVAC verifiable professional identity and certificate
verified_sources.domain_signal: hospitality, travel, tourism and visitor-services domains

verified_sources.name: Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security structure
verified_claims: The ministry lists agriculture, fisheries, veterinary services, animal husbandry, agribusiness, rural development, climate, extension, food reserve and nutrition/safety departments.
certifications: No single ministry credential is inferred; profession-specific councils and qualifications remain separate.
verified_sources.domain_signal: agriculture, food, forestry, wildlife, veterinary and climate domains

verified_sources.name: Nigerian social-work professional context
verified_claims: The Nigerian Institute of Social Workers is used as the local professional reference for social-work role naming in the repository.
certifications: Professional registration details require direct council or institute document confirmation
verified_sources.domain_signal: social work, social welfare, youth and humanitarian domains

verified_sources.name: Nigeria Meteorological Agency and climate services
verified_claims: NiMet is the Nigerian meteorological source for weather and climate-service context used by the repository.
competencies: apply climate information to operational decisions
certifications: No independent professional credential inferred from this page
verified_sources.domain_signal: climate science, meteorology, agriculture, aviation and environmental domains

verified_sources.name: Nigerian upstream and midstream petroleum regulatory sources
verified_claims: NUPRC and NMDPRA are the Nigerian regulatory context sources for upstream and midstream/downstream petroleum operations in the repository.
certifications: Sector credentials must be linked to the issuing body; do not infer a licence from the regulator homepage
verified_sources.domain_signal: oil, gas, petroleum engineering and energy domains

verified_sources.name: Nigerian legal, immigration, diplomacy and IP source set
verified_claims: The repository uses the NBA and specialised Nigerian bodies for local legal, immigration and IP terminology; a legal practice licence must be distinguished from an association membership.
verified_sources.domain_signal: legal practice, compliance, tax, immigration, diplomacy and IP domains

verified_sources.name: Chartered Institute of Purchasing and Supply Management of Nigeria
verified_claims: CIPSMN is the Nigerian professional reference for purchasing and supply-management terminology used in the repository.
certifications: Professional membership and certification details require programme-level source confirmation
verified_sources.domain_signal: procurement, supply chain, logistics and commercial operations domains

verified_sources.name: Nigerian Academy of Science and national research sources
verified_claims: The Nigerian Academy of Science and linked national research bodies provide Nigerian research and science-sector context.
certifications: No general research practice licence inferred
verified_sources.domain_signal: scientific research, neuroscience, social science, advanced science and materials domains

verified_sources.name: Nigerian Psychological Association
verified_claims: NPA describes psychology development, training, research and psychosocial service delivery as its professional mission.
Its membership categories distinguish student, graduate, associate, full and fellow progression.
competencies: work within qualification and practice requirements
certifications: clinical psychology practice-licence context requires the relevant practice body
verified_sources.domain_signal: psychology, counselling, cognitive science and wellness context

verified_sources.name: Nigerian Fashion Council and FADAN
verified_claims: The Nigerian Fashion Council identifies itself as an NBTE-inaugurated sector skills council for the fashion value chain.
FADAN provides student, emerging-designer and professional membership routes and states aims around education and practice standards.
competencies: build a professional portfolio and business
certifications: sector-skills qualifications require the applicable NSQ or training provider
verified_sources.domain_signal: fashion, textiles, garments, styling and creative enterprise domains

verified_sources.name: Nigerian sports federation and sports-sector context
verified_claims: The repository uses Nigerian sports bodies as local terminology and sector context; specific coaching or management credentials require the issuing federation or institute.
verified_sources.domain_signal: sports management, exercise science and sports therapy domains

verified_sources.name: Nigerian public-health regulatory and public-health association sources
verified_claims: The Nigerian health regulator directory and NPHCDA are used for public-health and primary-health-care context; professional licences remain council-specific.
competencies: work within health policy and ethics
certifications: Profession-specific health registration must be verified against the relevant council
verified_sources.domain_signal: public health, community health, health policy and social-care domains

verified_sources.name: National Association of Hair and Beauty Practitioners of Nigeria
verified_claims: The association describes itself as a Nigerian hair and beauty practitioners body.
It states that it works to promote standards, professional development and sanitation in the sector.
competencies: deliver hair and beauty services safely
follow sector standards and professional conduct
verified_sources.domain_signal: hairdressing, barbering and beauty services

verified_sources.name: Association of Practitioners of Spa and Medical Aesthetics of Nigeria
verified_claims: APSMAN describes itself as a Nigerian professional organisation for spa and medical aesthetics practitioners.
It reports training, certification and licensing activity for members; this is not treated as a statutory medical licence.
competencies: apply hygiene, safety and ethical practice
verified_sources.domain_signal: beauty therapy, spa and medical aesthetics

verified_sources.name: Practitioners of Spa and Beauty Association of Nigeria
verified_claims: POSBAN describes a Nigerian association for spa, hair and beauty practitioners.
Its published rules reference training, qualification, sanitation and practice standards; membership is not treated as a statutory licence.
competencies: maintain safe salon and spa practice
verified_sources.domain_signal: hairdressing, barbering, beauty therapy and aesthetics

verified_sources.name: Council of Registered Builders of Nigeria, Construction Labour Market Information System
verified_claims: CORBON publishes National Occupational Standards for construction trades in Nigeria.
The published trade set includes plumbing in construction and painting and decoration.
competencies: install and maintain building plumbing systems
prepare, estimate and execute painting and decoration work
meet occupational performance criteria and evidence requirements
certifications: National Occupational Standards and National Skills Qualification routes
verified_sources.domain_signal: plumbing, pipefitting, painting and decorating

verified_sources.name: Chartered Institute of Professional Printers of Nigeria
verified_claims: CIPPON describes a Nigerian statutory institute for regulating and administering printing practice.
The governing Act provides for registration, approved qualifications and professional standards for printing practitioners.
skills: pre-press file preparation and plate production
competencies: prepare and manage print production work
work within registration and practice requirements
certifications: CIPPON professional registration and membership categories
verified_sources.domain_signal: printing technology, pre-press and print production

verified_sources.name: Society of Printing Practitioners of Nigeria
verified_claims: SPPN describes a Nigerian printing professional body covering printing, packaging, publishing and graphic communication.
It advertises training, certification, professional support and membership activity.
competencies: apply quality and professional practice standards
verified_sources.domain_signal: printing technology, pre-press and packaging

verified_sources.name: Standards Organisation of Nigeria, Product Certification
verified_claims: SON publishes Nigerian standards and product conformity and certification schemes.
The source covers materials, products, laboratories and quality assurance; it does not create an individual craft licence.
competencies: interpret and apply relevant Nigerian Industrial Standards
support quality control and certification processes
verified_sources.domain_signal: glass, ceramics, building materials and manufacturing quality

verified_sources.name: Building Materials Producers Association of Nigeria
verified_claims: BUMPAN describes a Nigerian association representing building-material producers.
It provides sector advocacy and industry context; it is not treated as a personal professional licensing body.
verified_sources.domain_signal: building materials, manufacturing and construction supply

verified_sources.name: Nigerian Institute of Building
verified_claims: NIOB describes a Nigerian professional organisation for the building profession.
Its public material references built-environment practice and building-material standards work.
verified_sources.domain_signal: building materials and construction practice

verified_sources.name: National Association of Funeral Directors Education
verified_claims: NAFD publishes a funeral-service education framework with entry, operational and funeral-directing routes.
This is international learning and role evidence only; it is not a Nigerian licence or Nigerian regulator.
certifications: NAFD funeral-service education and DipFD routes
verified_sources.domain_signal: funeral services and funeral directing

quality_gate: Do not regenerate SQL or seed data from this audit alone.
Use source-specific skills and competencies only where the source names them or clearly defines the work.
Use generic global taxonomies for role normalization, never as Nigerian licensing or demand evidence.
Keep local regulator, professional association and government-context evidence visibly distinct in the UI and data model.
